visible_surface_condition: clean, smooth, cylindrical body with slight curvature
evidence_used: Visual appearance of a standard 1000 mL (33.8 fl oz) plastic hand sanitizer pump bottle
Smooth rigid plastic cylindrical container body allowing good parallel-jaw contact
Estimated total mass of approximately 1.0 kg to 1.1 kg including contents
High-friction silicone pad characteristics on rigid parallel-jaw fingers
calculation_summary: Estimated required normal force F_n = (Mass * Gravity) / (2 * mu), assuming object mass ~1.05 kg, gravitational acceleration ~9.81 m/s^2, and an estimated silicone-to-plastic static friction coefficient mu ~ 1.5. F_n = (1.05 * 9.81) / (2 * 1.5) = 10.3 / 3.0 ~ 3.43 N, rounded to 3.5 N for safety margin.
assumptions_and_uncertainty: Object mass is visually estimated from bottle scale as approximately 1 kg
Friction coefficient is approximated based on standard silicone-plastic pairs without direct slip testing
Uncertainty exists regarding exact dynamic load shifts if liquid sloshes during lift
reasoning_trace: The visual input shows a large pump bottle of hand sanitizer with a smooth plastic cylindrical body. The silicone gripper is well-suited for this geometry because the parallel flat-ish contact areas provide sufficient friction against smooth plastic. Given an estimated full bottle mass of roughly 1.0 kg, standard friction calculations dictate that a normal force of around 3.5 N is adequate to prevent slip against gravity under standard parallel-jaw closure without excessive crushing of the plastic container.
